memory_lessons.applicability: Relevant when comparing alternative AVX2 Base64 implementations under the same native protocol; the measurements do not isolate a single cause.
memory_lessons.claim: The observed valid paired-block candidate measured 17.93 µs and the valid range-classification candidate measured 22.43 µs. SIMD range classification alone therefore did not establish a speedup over the other candidate; a distinct packing implementation needs its own measurement.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this pairwise multiply-add packing candidate with the same correctness cases and repeated native timing; make no performance claim before those results.

proposal.hypothesis: The recorded range-classification AVX2 candidate was valid but measured at 22.43 µs, while a paired-block candidate measured 17.93 µs. Replacing shift/mask-based bit assembly with AVX2 pairwise multiply-add packing and lane interleaving may reduce packing work; classification overhead, stores, or tails could erase any gain. This candidate keeps bounded full-block accesses and uses scalar decoding when its vector or safe-quartet paths cannot accept the input.

retained: Retained the original scalar decoder under an internal reference name to preserve fallback behavior for malformed inputs.
Added an AVX2-targeted full-block decoder with vector range masks and arithmetic offsets for the Base64 alphabet; invalid vector blocks fall back to the reference path.

Replaced per-output-bit assembly with AVX2 pairwise multiply-add packing, saturating pack operations, and lane-local byte interleaving; loads are bounded to 32 input bytes and exactly 24 output bytes are copied per block.

Decoded the residual input in bounded four-character quartets, preserving terminal padding while avoiding wide scalar stores on valid short inputs and tails; unrecognized input falls back to the original decoder.

proposal.hypothesis: The measured AVX2 candidates do not isolate mapping cost: the valid single-block candidate averaged 22.43 µs and a paired-loop candidate 17.93 µs. This experiment tests whether forming one per-byte arithmetic offset from the existing mutually exclusive range masks, then adding it to the input vector, is faster than separate class-specific arithmetic mappings. The combined offset may reduce mapping instructions but add dependency depth; short inputs and tails should remain unaffected.

retained: Moved standard headers, including <cstring>, before their first use to address the known build diagnostic.

Replaced separate class-specific sextet arithmetic with per-class arithmetic offsets combined under the existing AVX2 range masks, followed by one vector byte addition; retained vector packing and all scalar, tail, padding, dispatch, and bounded memory paths.
